title: Air India Adds Mumbai-Toronto Route as Carrier Reshuffles North American Network
excerpt: New three-times-weekly service on upgraded 777-300ER starts October 25, even as airspace closures force summer schedule cuts across US routes.
body:
• Air India launches new Mumbai-Toronto route starting October 25, operating three times weekly on upgraded Boeing 777-300ER aircraft with first class suites and flat-bed business class
  • The carrier is maintaining 33 weekly flights to North America despite temporarily suspending Delhi-Chicago, Delhi-Newark, and Mumbai-JFK routes this summer due to airspace closures over Iran, Pakistan, and Russia
  • More than 8.7 million passengers fly between India and North America annually, with over 85% traveling indirectly — underscoring massive demand for direct connectivity
  • Fleet-wide cabin upgrades are underway, with 787 retrofits expected through late 2026 and 777 refurbishments to follow

Air India has confirmed a new ultra-long-haul route connecting Mumbai's Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj International Airport to Toronto Pearson, marking the carrier's latest move to expand direct connectivity between India and North America. The service begins October 25 and will operate three times weekly — on Wednesdays, Fridays, and Sundays — through March 26, 2027.

New Route Details

The Mumbai-Toronto flights will use the 328-seat Boeing 777-300ER with upgraded cabins: eight first class suites with privacy doors in a 1-2-1 configuration, 40 flat-bed business class seats, and 280 economy seats. Wi-Fi, improved in-flight entertainment, and better catering are part of the package, according to Air India's announcement.

https://youtube.com/watch?v=wE81aWMr9T8

Westbound flights depart Mumbai at 4:00 AM local time, arriving in Toronto at 10:00 AM — a block time of roughly 16 hours and 30 minutes. Eastbound, flights leave Toronto at 12:30 PM and land in Mumbai at 2:10 PM the next day, about 15 hours and 10 minutes.

Air India says the flights will be nonstop. However, aviation analysts at Simple Flying note that the airline's existing Mumbai services to JFK and Newark currently require a refueling stop in Rome due to airspace detours around Iran, Pakistan, and Russia — and the Toronto route may face the same constraint.

Filling a Ready-Made Market

The timing is strategic. Air Canada operated between Toronto and Mumbai via London Heathrow during the winter 2025/2026 season but has since pulled out. Air India is stepping into a market that handled 128,000 round-trip passengers in the 12 months to May 2026, according to booking data cited by Simple Flying.

"Travel between India and North America is characterized by high passenger volume, relatively low yields, and most of the traffic flying indirectly via European and Gulf hubs."

— Simple Flying analysis, August 2026

Toronto is already served by Air India from Delhi, but the India-Toronto market is large — more than 1.2 million round-trip passengers annually, or roughly 3,300 travelers daily. The new Mumbai service will particularly target passengers from western and southern India, including Ahmedabad (81,000 annual passengers to Toronto), Bengaluru (49,000), Hyderabad (47,000), and Chennai (41,000), who can connect through Mumbai.

Summer Network Cuts and Consolidation

The new route comes amid a significant reshuffling of Air India's international schedule. The carrier temporarily suspended its Delhi-Chicago, Delhi-Newark, and Mumbai-JFK services for the June through August 2026 period, according to Air India's official network notice. Several other routes saw frequency reductions: Delhi-San Francisco dropped from 10 to 7 weekly flights, Delhi-Toronto from 10 to 5, and Delhi-Vancouver from 7 to 5.

The cuts stem from a confluence of pressures. The 2026 Iran crisis disrupted Middle Eastern airspace, forcing Air India's long-haul flights to reroute through Europe and stretching block times to as long as 22 hours. Surging jet fuel prices and a fleet shortage — driven by the ongoing retrofit of 26 Boeing 787-8 aircraft — have compounded the challenge.

Despite the reductions, Air India says it is maintaining 33 weekly flights to North America and more than 1,200 international flights per month. Mumbai-Newark has actually increased from three to seven weekly flights, and Delhi-JFK retains daily service on the Airbus A350.

What It Means for Diaspora Travelers

For Indian Americans and the broader diaspora in Canada, the changes are a mixed bag. Fewer nonstop options this summer mean fuller planes and greater reliance on one-stop itineraries via European or Gulf hubs. But the Mumbai-Toronto addition and the Mumbai-Newark frequency boost signal Air India's commitment to routes with the heaviest diaspora demand.

Cabin upgrades offer a silver lining. Air India's A350s — currently flying Delhi to London, Newark, and JFK — already feature the carrier's new product with private lie-flat business class. The ongoing 787 retrofits are expected to be completed by late 2026, with 777 upgrades wrapping up by end of 2027, according to CEO Campbell Wilson.

Air India has described the summer schedule cuts as tactical rather than structural and plans to restore frequencies as conditions permit. For now, the carrier is concentrating capacity where demand and yields are strongest — a strategy that, if executed well, could strengthen its position against the Gulf carriers that currently dominate India-North America routing.
